selected_result: Ordering property of the Cholesky factor under complete pivoting

bibliographic_source.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., Chapter 10: Cholesky Factorization, Problem 10.7

paper_locations.anchor: Problem 10.7: equation (10.13), stated on the page introducing the standard pivoting strategy

task_clarification: Let A be positive semidefinite of rank r, and let the Cholesky decomposition with complete pivoting produce the factor R.
Formalize equation (10.13): r_kk^2 >= sum_{i=k}^{min(j,r)} r_ij^2 for j = k+1:n and k = 1:r.
In particular the diagonal entries satisfy |r_11| >= |r_22| >= ... >= |r_rr|.
The pivoting strategy is the standard one: at each step the pivot is the largest remaining diagonal entry.
scope_constraints: A is positive semidefinite of rank r; complete pivoting is the strategy defined by the source.
This is an exact algebraic property of the factor, not a rounding-error bound.
State the index ranges exactly as given.
Represent the pivoted factorization rather than assuming the inequality.
